patches.value: Let J=[r/2,3r/2] and take compact C from H003. M005 gives compact C×J. The continuous e_t is bounded there by K and vanishes outside C. C is measurable and has finite Lebesgue measure. M008 gives integrability on C of the constant function K; M009 then gives integrability on ℝⁿ of b=K·1_C. For F(τ)(x)=e(x,τ) and F′(τ)(x)=e_t(x,τ), each F(τ) is strongly measurable by continuity. The support and integrability result already proved gives integrability of e(·,r); smoothness makes F′(r) continuous and strongly measurable. Smoothness also gives the pointwise parameter derivative, and |F′(τ)(x)|≤b(x) for all x and τ∈J. M006 therefore applies and gives that E is differentiable at r with E′(r)=∫e_t(x,r)dx. Since r is arbitrary, this holds at every positive time.
